Fig. 7
Entry of carbon skeletons into the TCA cycle. In addition to acetyl CoA for oxidation the TCA can use acetyl and other substrates for
oxidation or as part of other pathways such as gluconeogenesis. Leucine and lysine are shown in parentheses since these amino acids only give rise
to acetoacetate (a 4 carbon molecule equivalent to two acetyl CoA) and therefore cannot be used for gluconeogenesis. The entry of propionate (3
carbons) is also shown since this is the only fatty acid that can be used for gluconeogenesis.
